# Skill: unifi

# Unifi

## Company and Brand

**Ubiquiti** is a leading networking company that targets the prosumer marketplace while trending to larger and larger business needs. It's flagship brand is **Unifi**.

::summarize company.md length="1 paragraph"

If you want more details on **Ubiquiti** as a company or the **Unifi** brand, read: [Unifi Brand Details](brand.md).

## Service Offerings

### Network

The **Network** service offering is the most mature part of the **Unifi** suite and what most people immediately think of when they hear the name **Unifi**. To find out more about the offering as well as the mobile app that supports the Network offering read [Network Service and Application](service-offerings/network.md).

The network service is also fully supported on the [Unifi Web Application](apps/web-app.md).

If you want the specs for a particular product in the network service, you will find it in one of the following links:

- [Unifi Routers and Gateways](products/routers.md)
- [Unifi Switches](products/switches.md)
- [Unifi Access Points](products/ap.md)

### Protect

The **Protect** service line helps users to capture, observe, and manage security feeds. For details on this service offering as well as the **Protect** mobile application read [Protect Service and Mobile Application](apps/protect.md).

Like the network service, the **Protect** service offering is fully supported by the [Unifi Web Application](apps/web-app.md) in addition to the mobile app.

While the **Protect** service offering is more than just security cameras, if what you're looking for is the specs of a particular security camera you'll find them all here: [Unifi Security Cameras](products/security-cameras.md).

### Access

The **Access** service line helps users interact with physical security devices like door locks, gates, and more. For more details on this service offering as well as the mobile app supporting it you should read: [Unifi Access Service and Mobile Application](service-offerings/access.md).

### Connect

The **Connect** service line

### Talk

## Products

### Routers

The ever popular "UDM (Unified Dream Machine)" and "UDM Pro" lines continue to be big hits in the WAN/Routers space for Unifi but their product offering continues to grow.

To find out more details on all of the routers Unifi provides, read: [Unifi Routers](products/routers.md)

### Switches

**Unifi** offers a huge lineup of managed switches which are all exposed in the [Network Application](apps/network.md). For details on the switches that **Unifi** offers read: [Unifi Switches](products/switches.md).

### Security Cameras

A big part of the **Protect** service line is providing security camera footage along with the associated events and metadata in a meaningful way. To find out more about security cameras which **Unifi** provides, read: [Security Cameras](products/security-cameras.md).

> **Note:** security cameras include specialized equipment like doorbell cameras, etc.

## APIs

Unifi has recently been introducing and improving a set of API's that helps developers integrate with their Unifi hardware. To find out more about these APIs read: [Unifi APIs](api.md).

### Does UniFi Talk phones integrate with Zoom?

Yes, G3 Talk phones can be used with Zoom Phone. Learn [How to Use UniFi Talk G3 Phones with Zoom](https://help.ui.com/hc/en-us/articles/34357014321431-Using-UniFi-G3-Phones-With-Zoom).

For troubleshooting help with the Zoom Integration, please refer to the [Zoom Configuration Guide](https://support.zoom.com/hc/en/article?id=zm_kb&sysparm_article=KB0074333#h_2933376925101709765412545).

---

### Do UniFi Talk phones have the necessary features to replace my existing systems?

UniFi G3 phones support Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) and remote configuration via Talk Relay hosted on UniFi Official Hosting. Later this year, we plan to introduce API and redirect server capabilities to provide even greater flexibility for professional installers.

---

### Does UniFi Talk have integrations with other product lines?

Yes, Talk phones can unlock door access systems adopted to UniFi Access and view security camera footage from UniFi Protect.

---

### What hardware is required to use UniFi Talk?

-   For local PBX setups, we suggest a compatible UniFi Cloud Console-we recommend a [UniFi Cloud Gateway](https://ui.com/us/en/cloud-gateways), such as the [Dream Machine Pro](https://store.ui.com/us/en/category/cloud-gateways-large-scale/products/udm-pro?s=us&l=en) or [Special Edition](https://store.ui.com/us/en/category/cloud-gateways-large-scale/products/udm-se?s=us&l=en), to leverage the built-in internet gateway and firewall for optimal performance. A [UniFi CloudKey+](https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/physical-security/uck-g2-plus) can be used for installations where only Talk phone management is required.
    
-   Note: A hard disk drive (HDD) is required to store call recordings, but UniFi Talk will still function without one.
    
-   For 3rd party PBX setups, you must bring your own PBX and configure your UniFi Talk G3 phones using SIP credentials.
    

---

### How much does it cost to deploy UniFi Talk?

In addition to the cost of your devices, we offer UniFi Talk service (SIP) services in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom for seamless calling with local phone numbers when using Talk PBX on UniFi OS Consoles. Pricing varies by region.

UniFi does not charge additional licensing fees. You'll always know exactly what you're paying for.

---

### Can I try UniFi Talk service (SIP) for free?

Yes, we offer a 15-day free trial for up to two UniFi Talk numbers when installing UniFi Talk on the UniFi OS Console. To start your trial, set up UniFi Talk and connect up to 2 devices. Your trial period will begin when you complete the setup process and configure your numbers.

If you bring your own PBX, you can enjoy a 30-day free trial of UniFi Official Hosting, during which you can install Talk Relay to remotely manage up to 100 Talk G3 phones.

---

### What are the features and subscription fees in the United States for UniFi Talk service (SIP)?

**Plus Plan**

Cost: $9.99 per month/per number

Included Features:  

-   3,000 monthly minutes per number (for worldwide inbound calls and outbound calls to the US, Canada, and Mexico)
-   50 monthly SMS messages per number (for messages sent and received in the US, Canada, and Mexico 60 call transcription minutes per number)
-   Unlimited concurrent calls per number
-   Emergency calling
-   Free number porting

**Pro Plan**

Cost: $24.99 per month/per number

Included Features:  

-   Unlimited voice (for worldwide inbound calls and outbound calls to the US, Canada, and Mexico)
-   Unlimited SMS (for messages sent and received in the US, Canada, and Mexico)
-   600 call transcription minutes per number
-   3,000 caller ID name (CNAM) lookups
-   UniFi Identity softphone
-   All Plus Plan features included, such as unlimited concurrent calls, emergency calling, and free number porting.

---

**Additional Details:**

Monthly Minutes and SMS Pooling:  

-   Plus Plan: Minutes and SMS messages are pooled across all numbers in the subscription. Usage beyond the pool is charged at $0.02/min (calls) or as per the rates table (SMS).
-   Internal extension calling is free and does not require a UniFi Talk subscription.

Call Transcription Minutes:

-   Transcription minutes are shared by all Plus and Pro Plan numbers in the subscription.

Emergency Calling:

-   VoIP 9-1-1 service differs from traditional telephone 9-1-1 services.

Pro Plan Restrictions:

-   It is designed for regular business use. High-volume calling (e.g., call centers, auto-dialing, trunking) is not allowed. Ubiquiti may suspend or terminate service for misuse.

CNAM Lookups (Pro Plan Only):

-   Caller ID name lookups are pooled across all Pro Plan numbers. Additional lookups beyond the monthly limit are charged at $0.01 per lookup.

For more details, please refer to the [help article](https://help.ui.com/hc/en-us/articles/29247192941335-UniFi-Talk-Relay-FAQs).

For detailed rates for international calls or SMS, please refer to the [UniFi Talk service (SIP) rates table](https://ui.com/us/en/integrations/managed-voip/international-rates?country=US).

---

### What are the features and subscription fees in Canada for UniFi Talk service (SIP)?

-   50 monthly SMS messages per number (for messages sent and received in the US, Canada, and Mexico)

-   600 call transcription minutes per number
-   UniFi Identity softphone
-   All Plus Plan features included, such as unlimited concurrent calls, emergency calling, and free number porting

---

-   Minutes and SMS messages are pooled across all numbers managed by your UniFi Talk subscription. Usage beyond the pool is charged at C$0.02/min for calls in the US, Canada, and Mexico, or as per the rates table for SMS and international calls.
-   Internal extension calling is free and does not require a UniFi Talk subscription.

-   Emergency calling
-   Free number porting

-   International calls are charged as per the rates table.

---

### What are the features and subscription fees for international users?

UniFi Talk seamlessly integrates with third-party SIP providers, enabling businesses to maintain their existing SIP provider relationships while taking advantage of UniFi Talk’s robust features.

Integration Templates:

Pre-configured templates for popular SIP providers, including:  
Breeze Connect, Deutsche Telekom, easybell, DIDWW, Telnyx, VoIP.ms.  
Additional templates are coming soon, making the setup process even easier.

For more information on integrating third-party SIP providers, visit Adding a [Third-Party SIP Provider](https://help.ui.com/hc/en-us/articles/18020323453847-Adding-a-Third-Party-SIP-Provider-to-UniFi-Talk).

---

### Do I have to purchase a UniFi Talk number for each device?

Subscription **locked** phones must be assigned to a user with a unique, directly assigned UniFi Talk number and have an internet connection to function. These phones can share numbers with groups after assignment to an eligible user. Subscription locked phones are ideal for configurations where users are assigned a unique number to make and receive calls. For example, an installation with 20 phones assigned to users, each with a unique, individual phone number (i.e., 20 total phone numbers), can benefit from a lower initial hardware cost when using subscription locked phones.

Subscription **unlocked** phones are ideal for configurations where users only share numbers with groups. These phones do not require assignment to a user with a unique, directly assigned UniFi Talk number nor do they require an Internet connection to function. For example, an installation with 20 phones sharing a single phone number should use subscription unlocked phones.

Internal calls between UniFi Talk users are free and do not require a subscription.

---

### I want to transfer my current numbers to UniFi Talk. How can I submit a number porting request?

You can submit number porting requests in the UniFi Talk application. [Learn more](https://help.ui.com/hc/en-us/articles/4407676051351-UniFi-Talk-Number-porting) about UniFi Talk number porting.

Within the United States, UniFi Talk supports the porting of nearly all numbers. Currently, UniFi Talk does not support toll-free numbers and numbers associated with rate centers in very select geographic regions. If you want to validate the portability of specific numbers, please [contact Ubiquiti support](https://account.ui.com/mysupport). Be sure to include the particular numbers you’d like to validate in your request.

---

### Do I need rollover lines in UniFi Talk?

No, you don’t need rollover lines in UniFi Talk because every UniFi Talk number supports unlimited concurrent calls. For example, if you have 10 users in a group that share a number, they can all make and receive calls simultaneously using that single, shared number. We designed UniFi Talk with flexibility in mind, so you only pay for exactly what you need.

---

### Can I use UniFi Talk phones with my PBX without Talk Relay?

G3 Talk phones can work with third-party PBX solutions without using Talk Relay. SIP credentials can be configured directly via the phone's touchscreen, but we suggest using Talk Relay (Part of UniFi Official Hosting) for maximum ease of use.

---

### Where can I get Talk Relay?

Talk Relay is included in our [UniFi Official Hosting](https://store.ui.com/us/en/category/accessories-advanced-hosting/products/unifi-hosting?s=us&l=en) service. Users purchasing an UniFi Official Hosting subscription can adopt UniFi devices from different product lines (Network and Talk) on the same UniFi Official Hosting site, providing maximum flexibility.

---

### What happens if I cancel my UniFi Official Hosting subscription?

Your configured phones will continue to function with a valid PBX configuration. However, access to Talk Relay's remote management and troubleshooting tools will no longer be available. SIP configurations can still be updated directly through the phone's touchscreen.

---

### Do G3 Talk phones work with my PBX?

G3 Talk phones are compatible with any PBX that adheres to the standard SIP protocol and does not require proprietary firmware. Verified compatible providers include RingCentral, Zoom, Voip.ms, Freeswitch, Nextiva, Asterisk, CallCentric, 3CX, and others.

3. **G3 Touch Wall** (UTP-G3-Touch-Wall) — $399.00 — "Next-generation wall-mountable smartphone for UniFi Talk, featuring a 7" touch display..." — OOS Aug 21, no restock date yet. Marked "New".
4. **G2 Touch Max** (UTP-TouchMax) — $249.00 — "Premium desktop smartphone that delivers the ultimate user experience." — "No restock date yet" (out of stock). Variant utp-touchmax-u.
5. **G2 Touch** (UTP-Touch) — $129.00 — "Versatile desktop smartphone that eliminates the learning curve." — Available (Select — multiple variants, subscription locked/unlocked presumably).
6. **G3 Wireless Handset** (UT-G3-Handset) — $99.00 — "Wireless handset which supports clear, high-quality audio for G3 Touch Phones." — In stock. This is an accessory for G3 phones.
7. **Analog Telephone Adapter** (UT-ATA) — $99.00 — "Easy-to-deploy adapter for managing analog telephones and fax machines with UniFi Talk." — In stock.

So the "Managed VoIP" (Talk) category has 7 items: 5 phones (3× G3, 2× G2), 1 wireless handset accessory, 1 ATA accessory.

The marketing page confirmed G3 specs:
- G3 Touch Enterprise: 7" touchscreen, desktop, 256.5 × 139.5 × 185.3 mm, Ethernet + WiFi, ergonomic handset with mute button, wireless handset support, high-performance speaker, Bluetooth support, 3rd party PBX support, internal video calling.
- G3 Touch Wall: 7" touchscreen, wall mount, 254.4 × 202.5 × 70.1 mm, Ethernet + WiFi.
- G3 Touch Pro: 5" touchscreen, desktop, 165.4 × 139.5 × 185.3 mm, Ethernet + WiFi.
- G3 Wireless Handset: 186 × 53.8 × 54.7 mm, works with G3 Touch phones.

Note the checklist row layout on the marketing page: "Ergonomic Handset with Mute Button / Wireless Handset Support / High-Performance Speaker / Bluetooth Support / 3rd Party PBX Support" — these appear once, probably applying to all three G3 phones (the columns are Enterprise, Wall, Pro). 8: # UniFi Protect Cameras
9: 
10: Ubiquiti sells roughly three dozen cameras under the UniFi brand, from a $99 PoE doorbell to a $1,999 31× optical-zoom PTZ with LiDAR autofocus. Every one of them is adopted by the same UniFi Protect application, every one is NDAA-compliant, and none of them carries a per-camera, per-seat, or per-recorder license — [Protect stores footage locally on your own console and charges nothing recurring for it](https://help.ui.com/hc/en-us/articles/31234972188951-How-UniFi-Protect-Protects-Your-Data). What separates the models is sensor size, optical zoom, IR reach, the AI tier the silicon can run, and — much more often than buyers expect — the speed of the Ethernet port on the back.
11: 
12: This document covers every camera currently listed on [store.ui.com](https://store.ui.com), grouped by product family, with the specifications that actually determine what a given camera can see and what it costs you in switch budget.
13: 
14: > **Scope note.** Ubiquiti files sensors, sirens, speakers, alarm hubs, and the SuperLink family under the same "Physical Security" store category. Those are alarm and detection products, not cameras, and are excluded here. Recorders (UNVR, ENVR, Cloud Gateways) appear only where camera capacity is relevant to scale.
15: 
16: ## How to Read the Numbers
17: 
18: Ubiquiti publishes about thirty specifications per camera. Roughly nine of them change a buying decision.
19: 
20: **Sensor size matters more than megapixel count, and the lineup is 8MP almost everywhere.** Nearly every current 4K UniFi camera resolves the same 3840 × 2160 at 8MP. What differs is the physical sensor gathering the light: the G6 Pro and G6 Edge families use a 1/1.2" sensor, the standard G6 family and the AI Turret/Dome use 1/1.8", the AI Multi Sensor pair uses 1/2.8" per lens, and the older G5 Pro uses 1/2". A 1/1.2" sensor has roughly 2.2× the area of a 1/1.8", which is the entire reason a G6 Pro Turret ($479) exists next to a G6 Turret ($199) at identical output resolution. Buy sensor area, not pixels.
21: 
22: **The Ethernet port is the most-missed specification in the range, and it splits the G6 family in half.** The G6 Pro, G6 Edge, and every AI-series camera carry a **GbE** port. The standard G6 Turret, G6 Dome, G6 Bullet, G6 Mini Dome, G6 180, G6 Pro 360, and G6 PTZ carry a **10/100 MbE** port — as does the entire G5 range. All of them are 4K cameras. A 100 Mbps port is genuinely sufficient for a single H.265 4K stream plus a substream, but it constrains high-bitrate configurations and it forecloses future headroom on exactly the models most likely to be deployed in bulk.
23: 
24: **PoE class is the switch-budget constraint, and the spread is enormous.** UniFi cameras run from 4 W (G5 Bullet, G5 Flex, G5 Turret Ultra) to 51 W (both AI PTZ models). Standard PoE (802.3af) covers most of the G5 and standard-G6 range; PoE+ (802.3at) covers the G6 Pro, G6 Edge, G6 PTZ, AI Turret, AI LPR, and AI Multi Sensor 2; PoE++ (802.3bt) is required by the AI Multi Sensor 4 and both AI PTZ cameras. Twenty AI PTZ Industrials need a 1,020 W budget before you count anything else on the switch.
25:

# UniFi Talk Phones and VoIP Hardware

UniFi **Talk** is Ubiquiti's IP-telephony service: a PBX application that runs on a UniFi OS Console (or pairs with third-party SIP/PBX providers), plus subscription-based outbound calling in the US, Canada, and the UK. The hardware side of the service lives in the **Managed VoIP** category of the Ubiquiti store and currently consists of seven products: five touchscreen desk/wall phones split across two generations (**G3 Touch** and **G2 Touch**), a Bluetooth wireless handset, and an analog telephone adapter (ATA) for legacy phones and fax machines.

The phones are unusual in the VoIP market: each is a self-contained Android-style "smartphone" with its own octa-core processor, 32 GB of storage, integrated 5 MP camera (with privacy shutter), WiFi, and an app platform that reaches into the wider UniFi ecosystem — Talk phones can unlock doors adopted in UniFi Access, pull up live feeds from UniFi Protect cameras, and place internal one-touch video calls between each other. There are no per-device licensing fees; internal extension calling is free, and outbound calling is subscription-based (US$9.99–$24.99/month or £7.99/month per number, depending on plan and region).

> **Scope note.** This document covers the telephony hardware in the Managed VoIP store category: the phones themselves plus the two Talk-specific companion devices (G3 Wireless Handset, UT-ATA). Legacy, discontinued phone lines are summarized at the end for completeness. Consoles (Cloud Gateways, CloudKey+) that host the Talk application are out of scope.

> **Pricing basis.** Prices are Ubiquiti's list prices on [store.ui.com](https://store.ui.com/us/en/category/all-integrations) (USD) and [store.ui.com/uk](https://store.ui.com/uk/en/category/managed-voip) (GBP) as of **5 September 2026**. The US store separately displays a higher "surcharge included" figure; base list prices are quoted here. Stock status is noted per product.

## What Distinguishes the Phones From Each Other

Ubiquiti publishes a nearly identical spec block for every phone, which makes the handful of real differentiators easy to miss. Five axes separate the lineup:

**Generation (G2 vs G3) is the biggest divide.** The G3 series is the current generation, flagged "New" on Ubiquiti's Managed VoIP page. All three G3 models support **Talk Relay** (remote provisioning and management via UniFi Official Hosting), Zero Touch Provisioning, direct SIP configuration from the touchscreen with third-party PBXes (Zoom, RingCentral, 3CX, Asterisk, Nextiva, Voip.ms are verified), and **Bluetooth 5.2 LE audio** for the G3 Wireless Handset. The G2 phones carry only Bluetooth 4.2, are not listed for Talk Relay support, and cannot pair with the G3 Wireless Handset. Both generations work with the Talk PBX on a UniFi OS Console.

**Display size is the primary tier split within each generation.** A 7" 1280 × 800 panel (Enterprise, Wall, Touch Max) versus a 5" 720 × 1280 panel (G3 Touch Pro, G2 Touch). Screen size tracks the rest of the hardware tier almost perfectly.

**Audio hardware separates tiers as reliably as the screen.** The 7" models carry **dual 3 W hands-free speakers**; the 5" models carry a single 2 W speaker. All five phones share the same dual MEMS hands-free microphones, wideband handset audio, and dedicated mute button.

**Mounting orientation.** Four phones are desktop models with an ergonomic wired handset; the **G3 Touch Wall** is the only wall-mount model and ships without a wired handset or headset jack, operating as a hands-free speakerphone/video unit.

**Power draw and PoE class.** G2 Touch sips 8 W over standard PoE; G3 Touch Pro takes 10 W (PoE); the G3 Enterprise and Wall take 11 W; the G2 Touch Max tops out at 15 W and wants PoE+. All desktop phones expose dual GbE RJ45 ports so a PC can daisy-chain through the phone.

NFC is a minor differentiator (present on the two 7" G3s and the G2 Touch Max; absent on both 5" phones), as are colors (G3 ships black only; both G2 models ship in black or white).
